Key changes: - Introduced history synchronization callbacks for ScrumOrchestrator. - Enhanced `ScrumState` with a `messages` field for conversation tracking. - Added unit tests for history injection and saving workflows. - Updated GitHub tools to support `tool_context` in all `_run` calls. - Refined Git configuration for better SSH and HTTPS handling.

feat: Enhance Scrum Master capabilities and project analysis
This commit introduces significant enhancements to the Scrum Master agent and the overall project analysis capabilities.
Key changes include:
- **New Quality Guardian Agent:** A new agent, `QualityGuardian`, has been added to track and report on quality KPIs, including team effectiveness, result quality, maintainability, and security. - **Workflow Documentation:** The Scrum Master can now generate a UML diagram of the current workflow and gather proposals for improvements. - **Enhanced Budget Management:** The Scrum Master can now provide a cost breakdown of roles, recommend a sprint budget, and optimize the process based on the budget. The process overhead for improvements is now configurable. - **Security Hardening:** The `litellm` integration has been hardened by restricting proxy access to localhost and pinning the version to `1.34.3` or higher to address a known supply chain security incident. - **Pydantic State Management:** The agent's state is now managed using Pydantic models, providing type safety and a more structured approach. - **Comprehensive Testing:** A testing framework has been established with tests for all agents and tools, ensuring the quality and correctness of the agent's behavior.
These changes improve the project's quality, maintainability, and security, and provide better insights into the development process.

Refactor project structure, add Scrum Team agents, enhance workflows, update tools and state management.
Key changes: - Restructure directories and move templates from `docs/` to `spec-templates/`. - Introduce the `Scrum Team` agents with the `root_agent` delegating tasks to sub-agents. - Add tools for state, budget, backlog, GitHub integration, and quality management. - Improve agent prompts and safeguards for template usage. - Establish tests for agent functionality, tools, and callbacks.

eat: Containerize agent and implement real-time cost limits This commit introduces a complete architectural overhaul to improve security, reliability, and configuration management by containerizing the entire application stack. It also replaces the previous budgeting model with a single, strictly enforced, real-time cost limit. Key changes: • Docker-based Environment: ◦ The agent now runs in a dedicated Docker container, managed via docker-compose.yaml. ◦ This removes the need for a local Python virtual environment and simplifies setup, ensuring a consistent environment. ◦ The agent's source code is mounted as a read-only volume to prevent self-modification. ◦ The state repository path is now configured via STATE_REPO_PATH in the .env file and mounted as a writable volume, isolating agent state from the application code. • Flexible GitHub Authentication: ◦ An entrypoint.sh script now manages authentication within the container. ◦ Supports both a fine-grained GITHUB_TOKEN (preferred) and a GitHub App, selectable via environment variables. ◦ The gh CLI is now installed in the container to support this. • Real-Time Cost Enforcement: ◦ The budgeting system has been refactored to use a single SPRINT_USD_BUDGET. ◦ A new check_cost_budget_callback performs a synchronous, real-time check against the LiteLLM /budget/info endpoint before every LLM call. ◦ This provides a hard financial guardrail, preventing cost overruns due to reporting delays and eliminating the less reliable token-based limit. • Improved Setup and Tooling: ◦ The setup.sh and doctor.sh scripts have been updated to be Docker-aware, checking for Docker, .env configuration, and the state repo path. ◦ The run.sh script now orchestrates docker compose, simplifying the process of running the agent.
Refactor ScrumState model, improve state tools, and enhance state-based tests; add scripts for state validation and test orchestration; update Dockerfile with multi-stage build and testing stage.
Remove Scrum Team agents, tools, and related modules.
Add unit tests for budget API callbacks, improve logging setup, enhance configuration management, and update scripts for session handling and environmental defaults.
Sync spec templates and roadmap management, enhance Markdown parsing, and improve state and story synchronization workflows.
Add automatic ID generation for Epics, User Stories, and ADRs; integrate `upsert_adr` tool across agents; and introduce unit tests for ID generation

Add enhanced session handling, strengthen budget constraints, and improve UTF-8 safety.
Key changes: - Introduced session resumption logic in `run_agent.sh` and integrated it with `docker-compose`. - Improved `ScrumState` model with fields for GitHub integration and error tracking. - Enhanced LiteLLM budget enforcement with guardrails for token and USD limits. - Refactored text reading methods to replace invalid UTF-8 sequences with U+FFFD. Added tests to ensure robustness with invalid encoding cases. - Updated Docker and run scripts for better error handling and multi-stage builds.

Add history management and enhance GitHub tooling.
Key changes: - Introduced history synchronization callbacks for ScrumOrchestrator. - Enhanced `ScrumState` with a `messages` field for conversation tracking. - Added unit tests for history injection and saving workflows. - Updated GitHub tools to support `tool_context` in all `_run` calls. - Refined Git configuration for better SSH and HTTPS handling.
